name: Balcony Visual Preferences – Façade and Inside Views
description: Faithful replication with the paper's own stimuli: Akbari, Yazdanfar, Norouzian-Maleki & Hosseini (2025), "Balconies' visual preferences: The case of residential apartments in Tehran, Iran", PLOS ONE 20(7): e0324874. The stimuli are the paper's 56 Autodesk Revit model images (Figures 7 and 8, CC BY 4.0): 32 street views of one apartment façade whose balconies vary in location (middle or corner), placement, area (share of the façade) and parapet type (fence, solid or mixed), and 24 views from inside a balcony looking out, varying parapet and balcony configuration. Participants first rate all 32 façades, then all 24 inside views, each on a 1–5 scale from very unpleasant to very pleasant; ratings are keyed by image number so the paper's design parameters can be attached for analysis. Age, gender, home ownership, education and household size are asked at the start. In the paper (362 Tehran residents), the most pleasant façades had balconies covering 50–75% of the façade with simple parapets, and smaller balconies were rated unpleasant. Differences from the original study: (1) image order is randomised within each part, whereas the paper's questionnaire numbered the images 1–32 and 1–24; (2) the images are cropped from the published figures and are smaller than the originals; (3) income is not asked, and a question on whether the participant's home has a balcony is added; (4) the paper's Delphi expert rounds that chose the design parameters are not part of the template.
author: Akbari, Yazdanfar, Norouzian-Maleki & Hosseini
